verdict: The two pages are almost the same. Both use the same #F7F7F7 paper, the line pitch is almost the same (63px in A, 64px in B), and the measure is about the same (~1452px against ~1430px, both around 64–65 monospace characters). B puts a filename and two icons above the text, so there's always something on the page besides the words. A drops all of that, but its rounded corners show a sliver of another colour at both top corners, which looks sloppy once you notice it. I'd still rather write in the empty frame and live with the corner flaw than have a title bar in view the whole time.

states.name: light
states.gap: B's lines are slightly more cramped and its paper slightly darker. Body lines are 74 device px apart against A's 76 (about 1.80× against 1.85× the ~41 px glyph height, a 2.6% tighter leading), and the paper is #F7F7F7 against A's #F9F9F9. On a long screen the text block reads a little denser and greyer.
states.gapTheirs: A puts the heading hashes inside the text column instead of hanging them in the margin. The body's left edge is at x≈622 device px, but A's H1 words start at ≈672 px and its H2 words at ≈698 px, 50 and 76 px to the right of it. So the one vertical line the page is built on breaks at every heading. B hangs '#' and '##' to the left, starting at ≈545 px, so its heading words sit exactly on the 622 px body edge.
states.verdict: The two pages measure almost the same: body text starts at 622 px and wraps at about 2245 px on both, both are near-white, and both have generous side margins. That leaves the left edge as the deciding difference. A lets its heading markers push the headings out of line with the body, so the column wobbles at every section break. B hangs the markers in the gutter, and its left edge runs straight from top to bottom. A's extra 2 px of leading and slightly brighter paper don't make up for that.

states.name: short
states.gap: The measure is a little tighter and the lines sit a little closer. Glyph advance is ≈26.8 vs 26.4 device px per character (1134 vs 1118 display px over the same 61-character line), so a paragraph line wraps one word sooner ('empty,' / 'and'). Line pitch is ≈74 vs 76 device px, which makes the paragraphs look slightly more packed.
states.gapTheirs: The heading marker isn't hung in the margin. '# ' starts at x≈622 device px, on the same edge as the body text, so the heading words start about 51 px to the right of the body's left edge (≈673 vs 622). The text column's left edge breaks at every heading, and the left margin reads as 622 px for the body but 673 px for heading words.
states.verdict: Both pages use the same near-white paper and a centred column of about 1630 px with roughly 625 px of margin on each side. The real difference is the left edge. B hangs the '#' out in the margin, so heading and body share one straight edge at x=622. A pushes the heading words in by a marker's width, so the column's left edge jogs at every heading, and you notice it every time your eye goes back to the start of a line. B pays for that with slightly tighter lines and a wider advance that wraps a word early, but a crooked left edge is harder to ignore than 2 px of leading.
